15.18.18.en: "I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, Lord, only makest me dwell in safety" (Ps 4:8).

15.18.19.en: "The Lord will give strength unto his people; the Lord will bless his people with peace" (Ps 29:11).

15.18.20.en: "Let them shout for joy, and be glad, that favour my righteous cause: yea, let them say continually, Let the Lord be magnified, which hath pleasure in the prosperity of his servant" (Ps 35:27).

15.18.21.en: "But the meek shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace" (Ps 37:11).

15.18.22.en: "Mark the perfect man, and behold the upright: for the end of that man is peace" (Ps 37:37).

15.18.23.en: "He hath delivered my soul in peace from the battle that was against me: for there were many with me" (Ps 55:18).

15.18.24.en: "The mountains shall bring peace to the people, and the little hills, by righteousness" (Ps 72:3).

15.18.25.en: "In his days shall the righteous flourish; and abundance of peace so long as the moon endureth" (Ps 72:7).

15.18.26.en: "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them" (Ps 119:165).

15.18.27.en: "He maketh peace in thy borders, and filleth thee with the finest of the wheat" (Ps 147:14).

15.18.28.en: "For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee" (Prov 3:2).

15.18.29.en: "Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace" (Prov 3:17).

15.18.30.en: "The fear of the Lord is the crown of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish" (Sir 1:22).

15.18.31.en: "For if thou hadst walked in the way of God, thou shouldest have dwelled in peace for ever" (Bar 3:13).

15.18.32.en: "Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ" (Rom 5:1).

15.18.33.en: "For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace" (Rom 8:6).

15.18.34.en: "And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!" (Rom 10:15).

15.18.35.en: "For the kingdom of God is not meat and drink; but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit" (Rom 14:17).

15.18.36.en: "Let us therefore follow after the things which make for peace, and things wherewith one may edify another" (Rom 14:19).

15.18.37.en: "Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Spirit" (Rom 15:13).

15.18.38.en: "Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen" (Rom 15:33).

15.18.39.en: "And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly" (Rom 16:20).

15.18.40.en: "Grace be to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ" (1 Cor 1:3).

15.18.41.en: "But God hath called us to peace" (1 Cor 7:15).

15.18.42.en: "For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints" (1 Cor 14:33).

15.18.43.en: "And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace" (Eph 6:15).

15.19.0.en: "He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword." [22]

15.19.1.en: The wicked man is pursued by his evils; he loses all hope of coming out of the darkness that surrounds him. He lives in terror, as though the sword were poised over his neck, expecting to be killed from one moment to the next. For in the depths of his being he knows that "he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword" (Rev 13:10).

15.19.2.en: "They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace" (Jer 6:14; 8:11).

15.19.3.en: "We looked for peace, but no good came; and for a time of health, and behold trouble!" (Jer 8:15)

15.19.4.en: "Hast thou utterly rejected Judah? hath thy soul lothed Zion? why hast thou smitten us, and there is no healing for us? we looked for peace, and there is no good; and for the time of healing, and behold trouble!" (Jer 14:19)

15.19.5.en: "There is no soundness in my flesh because of thine anger; neither is there any rest in my bones because of my sin" (Ps 38:3).

15.19.6.en: "And the way of peace have they not known" (Rom 3:17).

15.19.7.en: "And the peaceable habitations are cut down because of the fierce anger of the Lord" (Jer 25:37).

15.20.0.en: "He wandereth abroad for bread, wherever he may find it, and knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand." [23]

15.20.1.en: The wicked man lives in wandering and emptiness, like one hungry for a crust of bread, unlike the righteous (Ps 37:23-25). And the day of darkness, or the day of judgment, is at the door, hastening toward him, and there is no postponement. The day of the Lord is light for the faithful believers, and darkness for the wicked, for they will be sentenced to the everlasting, outer, eternal darkness.

15.20.2.en: * When a man practices unlawful things, he fears what he has done!

15.20.4.en: * Because the rebel, our adversary, wages war with pride, and wants to conquer by arrogant exaltation, our victorious King gave us the weapon of humility.

15.20.5.en: Without the unconquerable power of humility, no one is victorious.

15.20.6.en: By humility the pride of the deceiver is bowed down, and he becomes a footstool for the feet of the meek and peaceable.

15.20.7.en: See how our mighty fathers opened the way for us: they put on humility, the garment of Christ, and overcame the wolf and bound him with the chains of darkness.

15.20.8.en: * The demons prepared for me a temptation that makes all who hear of it tremble...

15.20.9.en: In their impudence they return and show their cruelty toward me, threatening me.

15.20.10.en: And when I make before them the sign of the Cross, our life, they return to the darkness that is their portion, and their fire is quenched.

15.20.12.en: "Trouble and anguish shall make him afraid.

15.21.0.en: They shall prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle." [24]

15.21.1.en: The wicked man is frightened by inward harm and distress of soul more than by outward trials. As the Apostle Paul says: "Indignation and wrath, tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil" (Rom 2:8-9). For whoever loses his attachment to God, the doors of an unbearable hell open within him. The wicked man may think that he has rid himself of his inner fears, but these fears reign over his heart, his mind, and his inner powers, and enslave him, so that with his whole being he becomes a captive, as to a cruel king ready with mighty, unconquerable armies. Whoever wants to regain his freedom should begin with inner freedom in Christ Jesus our Liberator, or with freedom through divine righteousness against evil.

15.21.2.en: * [Distress makes him afraid, and troubles besiege him, like a king preparing for battle.] In all that the wicked man does, the fence around him is made of affliction, calamity, and troubles, so that his soul is troubled with anxiety and misgivings. A man who secretly longs to keep the good things of others from them by force wearies and distresses himself with the thoughts of his heart, hoping that it will not be discovered. Another, having abandoned the truth, sets his mind to lie so as to deceive the minds of his hearers. But the greatest labor is to defend himself with enough caution that his deception may not be found out... For the way of truth is smooth, but the way of falsehood is rough. Therefore it was said through the prophet: [They teach their tongue to speak lies, and weary themselves to commit iniquity] (Jer 9:5).

15.21.4.en: * When a bird is caught, it is not necessary for its whole body to enter the net; it is enough that the net seizes only its foot, for this does not lessen the hunter's control over it.

15.21.5.en: So it is with Satan: if he wants to bring us into his snare, it is not necessary for him to control all of our conduct and our faith; it is enough for him to begin to control our conduct. "Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth... And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you."

15.21.6.en: * Satan is called strong, not because he is so by nature, but in reference to the authority that has come to him because of our weakness.

15.21.7.en: * What degradation is greater than that of Satan, who was puffed up? And what exaltation is greater than that of the man who wants to be humble? The first has come to crawl on the earth beneath our feet, and the second has been raised on high with the angels.

15.21.8.en: St. John Chrysostom * Now, my beloved, Satan has been slain, that tyrant who is against the whole world... Death no longer reigns, but life rules in the place of death, for the Lord says: "I am... the life" (Jn 6:14), so that everything has been filled with joy and gladness, as it is written: [The Lord reigneth; let the earth rejoice] (ج)... Now that death has been abolished and the kingdom of Satan has been destroyed, all things are filled with joy and gladness.

15.22.0.en: St. Athanasius the Apostolic "For he stretcheth out his hand against God, and strengtheneth himself against the Almighty." [25]

15.23.0.en: "Running upon him (rushing upon him), stiffnecked, with the supports of his shields arrayed (with his thick bucklers)." [26]

15.24.0.en: "Because he hath covered his face with fatness, and made collops of fat on his kidneys." [27]

15.24.1.en: When the wicked man stretches out his hand against God and exerts himself against the Almighty, he crushes himself by himself.

15.24.2.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem says that Eliphaz likens Job to the Accuser (Satan), who was a great commander, holding the first rank among the heavenly beings, and fell (Rev 12:7-9). He raised his hand against the Lord, and lost his mind by resisting God. Delusion swallowed him, that is, he was filled with pride. And he took a hostile stand toward God through haughtiness. He is like Satan, who strikes in battle and hides, putting his shield on his shoulders, bearing a hard heart, covering his face with its fat, that is, with prosperity; and since he stuffs his belly with the evil of sinners, he cannot lift up his face before the Creator. He lays two layers of fat on his thigh, that is, he exercises his power through two things: greed and indulgence in pleasures. But Eliphaz tried in vain to compare the righteous Job with the Accuser, Satan.

15.24.3.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that these expressions apply to the Antichrist, the very chief of the wicked, who, when he raises his hand against God, is said to "prevail," but only for a time, since he is permitted to be exalted and glorified, and is then punished without mercy forever. He stretches out his hand against God, meaning that he persists in doing evil, unconcerned about the judgments of God. As for his running against God with a thick neck, it means that he commits shameful deeds that anger the Creator. For such a man is said to run in doing evil with no enemy to hinder him. And the thickness of his neck is the wealth of pride, supported by storehouses that overflow as though they came from the flesh.

15.24.4.en: These expressions also apply, in the view of Pope Gregory (the Great), to the wicked man who arms himself with authority, exalts himself against God, and takes a stand against the commandments of the truth. He disregards the riches of God and arms himself with the vain riches of temporal things. He covers his face with fat, seeking the fat of temporal goods without having the fear of the Lord in him; he oppresses the poor and exalts himself with the power of temporal glory.

15.24.5.en: * All the proud carry haughty necks; they not only practice evils, but refuse to count them as evils. And when they are rebuked, they justify themselves.

15.24.6.en: * The wicked wage war against God, and the earthen vessels are shattered and become fragments; so men puff themselves up, depending on their own strength. This is the shield of which Job speaks concerning the wicked man. [He runs against God, on the stiff neck of his shield.] What is "the stiff neck of his shield"? It is the man who depends most of all on his own self-protection.

15.25.0.en: St. Augustine "And he dwelleth in desolate cities, and in houses which no man inhabiteth, which are ready to become heaps." [28]

15.25.1.en: "And he shall dwell in deserted communities and ruined houses that have become ruins" (v. 28 LXX). We may be surprised at the expression "deserted communities," because the word "community" comes from people gathering together, so how can it be deserted? Wherever there is a great crowd of the wicked, each of them feels isolated, because sin corrupts a man's relationship with his brethren and removes love from them. Each one feels as though there is no one to share his feelings, and no one who understands his depths.

15.25.2.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that the inhabitants of the house are the thoughts; for the wicked, their thoughts will find no rest, so that they feel that they are wreckage and ruins with no one dwelling in them.

15.26.0.en: "He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he prolong the perfection thereof upon the earth." [29]

15.26.1.en: The wicked man does not know the feeling of satisfaction and contentment; he is not enriched, but remains poor continually, with nothing to fill his inner emptiness, even if he possesses much outward wealth.

15.26.2.en: The wealth he gathered by evil passes away by another evil. All his riches dwindle until they vanish: "which came up in a night, and perished in a night" (Jon 4:10). [Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished] (Prov 13:11).

15.26.3.en: When the wicked man loses his sons and dies, strangers inherit from him.

15.26.4.en: "Neither shall he prolong the perfection thereof upon the earth," that is, the time of his enjoyment of his wealth will not be long. He exerts all his effort to leave his wealth to his sons after him, but he fails to accomplish that.

15.26.5.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) says that the wicked man suffers from inner emptiness and will never feel satisfied; even his being appears like a passer-by without fruit.

15.26.6.en: "The darkness shall not depart from him.

15.27.0.en: The flame shall dry up his branches, and by the breath of his mouth shall he go away." [30]

15.27.1.en: He lives as one in perpetual darkness, and he corrupts his children as children of darkness, so that they are like the branches of a tree that has dried up and been burned.

15.27.2.en: The text in the Septuagint reads something like this: "He shall not be able to escape from the darkness by any means: let the wind blow upon his flower, and it shall fall." It is as though it says: the wicked man falls into a darkness from which he cannot be delivered, while upon his offspring, or his flower, the wind blows and makes it fall without its turning into fruit.

15.27.3.en: What the Septuagint says about his flower appears in the Hebrew text as his "branches," which the hot winds dry up, the scorching wind that burns the crops.

15.27.4.en: By the breath of his mouth the wicked man passes away, for he dies suddenly. As it was said: "This night thy soul shall be required of thee" (Lk 12:20), and also: "The wicked is driven away in his wickedness" (Prov 14:32). And the love of the world passes away with the passing of the world.

15.27.5.en: * If the proud man wants to turn back from sin to righteousness, he must depart from the darkness. But since he does not seek the light of righteousness, he does not depart from the darkness.

15.27.7.en: "Let not him that is deceived trust in vanity:

15.28.0.en: For vanity shall be his recompence." [31]

15.28.1.en: A man often thinks that deceit and the ways of evil can save him. At the beginning they lead him astray, but he soon drinks from the cup of evil that he himself filled.

15.28.2.en: "Let this be the reward of mine adversaries from the Lord, and of them that speak evil against my soul" (Ps 109:20).

15.28.3.en: "The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but to him that soweth righteousness shall be a sure reward" (Prov 11:18).

15.28.4.en: "For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord" (Rom 6:23).

15.29.0.en: "It shall be accomplished before his time, and his branch shall not be green." [32]

15.29.1.en: Not only does he lose his wealth, but he quickly loses his life, like one who dies before his appointed time.

15.29.2.en: It is true that the wicked may live to old age, and holy, righteous people may die in early childhood. But the years of the wicked man are counted as nothing, for the years of his life are like ashes, while one day of the days of the saints is counted in the eyes of God as a thousand years.

15.29.3.en: "For a thousand years in thy sight are but as yesterday when it is past, and as a watch in the night" (Ps 90:4).

15.29.4.en: "But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day" (2 Pet 3:8).

15.29.5.en: Even his children, whom he thought would be among the great ones of this age, become dry branches that are "not green."

15.29.6.en: What is the branch that is not green but the spiritual fruit of the believer? If he walks in evil, the fruit of the Spirit of the Holy God dries up in him, and becomes a cause of judgment instead of a support.

15.29.7.en: * Job was hoping for this: that because of his sufferings and his patience he would receive from God the reward of his inheritance. Eliphaz says that his "cup," or harvest, will perish before its time (of harvest), surely meaning that he will perish before the time of reward. [And his branch (on the tree) shall not flourish]... Thus Eliphaz declares that Job, who is expecting very great benefits, awaiting them as though they were in his hands, will be disappointed and will obtain nothing of what he expected.

15.29.8.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem * [Before his days are fulfilled he shall perish, and his hands shall be withered] [32]... Probably the wicked man, in God's hidden foreknowledge, is not assigned a long life by God; for since he wants to live according to the flesh, he imagines that he lives many days. And since he cannot reach the age he seeks for himself, he appears as one who perishes before his days are fulfilled.

15.29.9.en: This statement can also be understood in another sense. We commonly see people who walk in evil and yet reach a very advanced old age. How then can it be said: [Before his days are fulfilled he shall perish], when we see among them people whose limbs tremble with old age, and yet their passions do not cease to bring their evils upon them? There are some who, after losing the way of life, turned back, and their conscience began to torment them, so they left their shameless ways, changed their deeds, resisted their old evils, fled from earthly things, and followed heavenly aims; but before they were established in these holy aims and in the mortification of the mind, they returned to what they were at the beginning, and fell into their evil habits that they had resolved to leave... For unless the heart is first established in heavenly desires by continual seeking and continual conversion, when it turns back to carry out outward things, it is uprooted from its steadfastness in good work.

15.30.0.en: "He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive." [33]

15.30.1.en: His children will be like the bitter unripe grapes that fall from the vine before they grow and ripen, and like the olive blossom that falls and does not turn into fruit. His children die in the dawn of their lives and do not attain what he desired for them.

15.30.2.en: * [His cluster is spoiled like a vine at the beginning of its blossoming, and like an olive tree casting its flower. For the company of hypocrites shall be barren.] Let us consider how the hypocrite is spoiled like a vine at the beginning of its blossoming, or like an olive tree casting its flower.

15.30.3.en: If a vine, when it puts forth its blossoms and a severe cold touches it through a sudden change of weather, loses all its moisture and greenness, so there are some who, after passing periods in evil, long for the ways of holiness; but before good desires are established in them, as we have said, a kind of prosperity in the present life comes upon them, and they are entangled by it in outward concerns, and as their mind is drawn away from the warmth of inward love, it is as though a cold came upon them, and everything that had begun to appear in them of the shoots of virtue is killed. For through earthly occupations the mind becomes exceedingly cold unless it is established within...

15.30.4.en: [And he shall be like an olive tree casting its flowers]: when the olive tree has blossomed and comes into contact with a thick fog, it is stripped of the fullness of its fruit. So also many who enter upon good works are greatly praised by those who see them, and when they find pleasure in their praise, a fog descends upon their thoughts, and they no longer distinguish with what intention they do this, and so they lose the fruit of their work through the fog of the love of praise.

15.30.5.en: It was well said by Solomon: [Let us rise early to the vineyards, to see whether the vines have blossomed, and the flowers have borne fruit] (Song 7:12). The vines blossom when the minds of believers offer good works, but they bear no fruit if in their aim they cannot overcome their sinful practice.

15.30.6.en: * Hypocrites seem fruitful and green in the eyes of their fellow creatures, but in the sight of the hidden Judge they appear fruitless and withered.

15.31.0.en: "For the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery." [34]

15.31.1.en: * Fire burns the tents when the heat of greed corrupts the thoughts.

15.31.2.en: The hypocrite's mind will not rest from thinking of evil; for as he pursues earthly things or the love of praise, he murmurs against what belongs to others, and runs panting that it may be his, and strives to show others to be wicked by comparison with himself, since he wants to appear holier than the whole world.

15.31.3.en: By making others despised, he tries to appear at all times worthy of honor. Therefore, seeking praise from his neighbor, he spreads the nets of his tongue in judging his fellow creatures, so that he may catch a good opinion of himself among those whom he seeks to please.

15.32.0.en: "They conceive mischief, and bring forth vanity, and their belly prepareth deceit." [35]

15.32.1.en: * [He conceives sorrows.] And what is the fruit of this? [Vanity comes upon him, and his belly bears deceit.] Or rather, "he will bear" from what comes of "deceit"; he bears deceit itself, by bearing things that are of no use and do not profit him at all.

15.32.2.en: If Eliphaz were thinking about all these things realistically, and if he had met deceivers here, he would not have thought in a truthful and sincere way, because the judgment of many deceivers is reserved for the ages to come. And if he is speaking of rewards to come, he wrongs Job in vain. In vain he was condemning him for his sorrows. For the splendor of this life often falls upon the slaves of greed, and the miseries of life upon the righteous. God did not decree this wrongly, but altogether rightly. For He does not grant the righteous man the splendor of this life, whose fullness is leaves of trees, whose strength is shadow, whose wealth is straw, and whose glory is smoke; but the righteous man is made worthy of the Kingdom of Heaven, of incorruption, of immortality, and of heavenly glory, in which a person rejoices with the angels. This is why, even if they wear themselves out with sweat and meet with many hardships, they do not blame the Judge, knowing that through these slight afflictions they receive the glory to come (2 Cor 4:17), which shall be revealed to us (Rom 8:18) from the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

15.32.3.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem * [They conceive woe and bring forth iniquity, and their womb prepares deceit.] A man conceives woe when he plans evil things, and brings forth iniquity when he begins to carry out what he planned.

15.32.4.en: By indulging in envy he conceives woe, and by uttering slanders he brings forth iniquity.

15.32.5.en: It is a great evil when the wicked man strives to show others to be wicked, so that he himself may appear holy, by showing others to be unclean.

15.32.6.en: We must bear in mind that the Holy Bible uses the term "belly" or "womb" for the "mind." It was said by Solomon: [The lamp of the Lord is the ways of men, searching all the inward parts of the mind] (Prov 20:27). By the term "womb" the mind is rightly understood, for as offspring are conceived in the womb, so thought is generated in the mind. And as flesh is found in the belly, so thoughts are in the mind. The womb of the hypocrite prepares deceits, for he is always conceiving in his mind great evils against his relatives, in keeping with his aim for himself of appearing innocent before all men.

15.32.8.en: Let me profit from the reproaches of those who reproach me!

15.32.9.en: * Unjustly did Eliphaz and his two friends accuse the righteous Job!

15.32.10.en: They measured out bitter accusations to him, and they became a cause of glory for him!

15.32.11.en: As for me, in my weakness allow me to profit from their accusations!

15.32.12.en: * They claimed that he is hiding behind wisdom, but wisdom is innocent of him, for his knowledge is vain, and his depths carry destructive winds!

15.32.13.en: Grant me, O Lord, knowledge from You; shine with Your light upon my depths, that my life may become a living witness, that I may speak only what I live by You and in You. Grant that Your Holy Spirit may blow within me, that the destructive evil spirits may not be able to slip into me!

15.32.14.en: Let every word be anointed with the anointing of the Spirit.

15.32.15.en: And let my life be salt to the earth!

15.32.16.en: * Grant me, O Lord, that Your fear may take the steering wheel.

15.32.17.en: My soul walks in the royal road.

15.32.18.en: I enjoy fellowship with the Bridegroom of my soul, the Way, the Truth, and the Life!

15.32.19.en: I turn neither to the right nor to the left!

15.32.20.en: For the steering wheel is in the hand of an almighty, wise, and loving Father!

15.32.21.en: * Be, O Lord, the keeper of my mouth, and set a strong door before my lips, that nothing may come out of it but what pleases You. Grant that my words may be in harmony with my depths and my conduct,

15.32.22.en: so that they may not be a witness against my iniquity and a cause of my condemnation!

15.32.23.en: * I return in my thought to Your wonderful works.

15.32.24.en: You created everything for my sake.

15.32.25.en: And You gave my father Adam mind and wisdom.

15.32.26.en: You wanted his offspring to be truly wise, that they might be counted Your children, imitating You!

15.32.27.en: Grant me the Wisdom who sits at Your right hand.

15.32.28.en: Give to me not according to my merit, but according to Your love!

15.32.29.en: * You long to gather together all Your believers, and that Your believers be gathered to You.

15.32.30.en: You long to shine with the light of Your wisdom upon all.

15.32.31.en: You want all to be as those who are in Your council.

15.32.32.en: You reveal Your surpassing mysteries to those who fear You.

15.32.33.en: * Grant me, O Lord, the spirit of wisdom that is from You.

15.32.34.en: Then I will not exalt myself with knowledge that is not from me, nor claim wisdom as if it were unique and lofty.

15.32.35.en: Let me honor every human being, and appreciate the gifts God has given him!

15.32.36.en: * That I may profit from every sincere counsel, grant me humility, that I may profit from the wisdom of all, if possible.

15.32.37.en: But I do not seek human consolations, for You are the heavenly Physician, the giver of true consolations.

15.32.38.en: I listen to Your voice through Your Church, and You are revealed before my eyes, and I enjoy the joy of Your mysteries!

15.32.39.en: I see You revealed in Your servants, and I receive Your gifts from Your hands through them!

15.32.40.en: You are the giver of gifts to humble hearts!

15.32.41.en: * I look at myself, and I perceive the truth of my weakness.

15.32.42.en: Who can be justified before You, O Holy One?

15.32.43.en: No one born of woman is accounted pure before You, even if he is but one day old!

15.32.45.en: And the heavenly ones are not pure before You!

15.32.46.en: Do not entrust anyone with my salvation but Yourself!

15.32.47.en: * I confess to You that I drink iniquity like water.

15.32.48.en: But You are the forgiver of sins, You are the rescuer of souls from corruption!

15.32.49.en: * Now, O Lord, look upon Your holy Church.

15.32.50.en: Grant to all, priests and people, to be kindled with love of continual learning.

15.32.51.en: May all walk, led by Your Holy Spirit, in the footsteps of the early holy Fathers.

15.32.52.en: Let there be no stranger among us, with a perverted mind.

15.32.53.en: But may all be one flock under one Shepherd, enjoying Your fruitful pastures!

15.32.54.en: May all enjoy the spirit of simplicity, so that there be no proud or hypocrite among them!

15.32.55.en: * Grant me not to judge anyone, for You alone are the searcher of hearts.

15.32.56.en: I often suppose of one who falls under the weight of trials that it is the fruit of his hidden evils.

15.32.57.en: Who can comprehend Your wisdom, O Savior, Lover of mankind?

15.32.58.en: Not everyone who suffers is a saint or a wicked man.

15.32.59.en: You alone allow prosperity or distress, and in both cases You seek nothing but our salvation and our glory!

15.32.60.en: * Our hidden glances at those who tempt crush them, but Your divine hand provides what is for the edification of those who believe in You.

15.32.61.en: * My God, You are the source of my peace, indeed You are peace itself; whoever possesses You, no terror and no anxiety will enter his life!

15.32.62.en: He fears neither the darkness nor the sword!

15.32.63.en: There is nothing to terrify him as long as You dwell in his depths!

15.32.64.en: But whoever runs after evil runs after a destructive mirage; he gains vanity and loses the truth, wandering and emptiness come upon him, and he comes to need a crust of bread.

15.32.65.en: Distress comes upon him, and the enemy of good reigns over him.

15.32.66.en: Let me flee to Your Cross, and I will see You tearing up the bond that is against me, freeing me from the slavery of the devil, and bringing him beneath my feet.

15.32.67.en: In humiliation that tyrant falls and is made a public spectacle!

15.32.68.en: * Yes, let me draw near to You, O wonderful Crucified One, and be united with You, and pride will find no place in me.

15.32.69.en: Pride is shattered, which shattered my soul, turned my paradise into a wilderness, and made my dwelling a ruin!

15.32.70.en: Deceit flees, and the ways of evil are closed before me.

15.32.71.en: There is no more famine in my soul, nor bloodshed surrounding me.

15.32.72.en: My vine is filled with clusters of Your love!

15.32.73.en: And my olive tree bears fruit, to overflow with the oil of Your grace!

15.32.74.en: My soul knows poverty no more, but bears, by Your Holy Spirit, joyful heavenly fruits.

15.32.75.en: The destructive fire of evil does not approach my tent, but it is kindled with the holy fire of Your Holy Spirit.

15.32.76.en: My whole being becomes glorified in You.

15.32.77.en: I become like the heavenly ones, Your servants, the flames of fire!
